props.heading: What is BearMinion?

steps.description: One command sets up the site and the editor. You're editing your first page before your coffee cools down.

props.heading: Edit the page, not a form about the page.
props.intro: The editor reads your theme's own schemas, so it can only write content your site actually renders. No orphan fields. No mystery settings.

props.heading: Fair questions, straight answers.

items.a: In your repo. One JSON file per page in content/pages/, the site settings in content/site.json, images in src/assets/uploads/. Review it in a pull request like any other change.
No. The editor and its API exist only in astro dev. Production gets a static build with no editor, no server and no database to poke.
items.q: Does the editor ship to my live site?

items.a: Anyone with the repo cloned and the dev server running. The editor only answers your own machine, so other sites and your coworker's laptop can't touch your content. Editing a live site without a clone is planned.
items.q: Who can edit, and from where?

items.a: Yes. Once the site is created, the template is yours: change its components and styles, or add a section type with a schema, defaults and a component. The editor picks it up. See [Building a theme](https://docs.bearminion.com/themes/).
items.q: Can I use my own design?

items.a: Anywhere that serves static files: Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, GitHub Pages or a server in your closet. The host runs npm run build and publishes dist.
Nothing. It is [MIT licensed](https://github.com/langehelp-software/bearminion/blob/main/LICENSE), and the site it creates is yours. Keep the $99 a month.
